question: Should the shipped agent-core `toError()` facade retain its legacy non-Error message semantics during deprecation, or may this PR intentionally change them?
rationale: Repository policy treats shipped plugin API behavior as compatibility-sensitive, and retaining the symbol alone does not settle whether its observable error representation may change.

options.title: Preserve facade semantics
options.body: Keep the old `toError()` implementation for external compatibility while using `toErrorObject()` directly in migrated internal callers.

options.title: Approve the semantic break
options.body: Land the new structured behavior only with explicit maintainer approval and a documented major-release or deprecation boundary for affected consumers.

recommendation.title: Preserve facade semantics
recommendation.body: Keep the old `toError()` implementation for external compatibility while using `toErrorObject()` directly in migrated internal callers.

likelyOwner.reason: They sponsored the linked refactor and implemented both the facade preservation and resolver follow-up, making them the best available owner for clarifying the intended compatibility contract.
